title: The Queen of Spain, the national anthem and the claque
summary: In Madrid the show had to stop for the national anthem whenever the Queen entered, and he explains the paid claque.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Oh, he was a big child. Now, getting back to Spain -- this Queen, she had a habit of coming to our theater after the opening -- after the opening would start, you know, and we'd be right in the middle of our big opening, the girls are dancing, the band's playing, the cymbal's flying, and she'd walk in -- well, the minute she makes her entrance into her box, everything must stop. You stop, the girl's got her leg up, you stop right there. And you stop and play the Spanish National Anthem and then she and everybody sits down. Then you proceed and pick up whereyou left off. And she did that -- we were in Madrid about six weeks and she at least came once a week and every time she came we'd have to stop -- she came in almost near the ending of the opening and we'd have to stop it. Sometimes we'd have to do it over. Somebody would say, "Do it

from the beginning." And that to us was a very big joke. You know, in Spain they had the claque. If you owned a theater and I own a theater, you have a big attraction at your theater, I'll send a group of 15 or 20 to go in your theater and every act that comes on they'll boo -- they'll boo everything that comes on. I'd pay them to do that -- they call that the claque. And we thought that was the funniest thing we ever saw in -- heard in our lives. Having to stop in the middle of the show to play the National Anthem -- so we had a great time in Spain.
